steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Coat a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray.

Whisk flour, white sugar, brown sugar, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt together in a large bowl until thoroughly combined. Briefly beat eggs together in a separate large bowl, then whisk in milk until smooth.
Add flour mixture to egg mixture in batches, alternating with persimmon pulp, mixing well after each addition. Stir in melted butter; transfer to the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into center comes out clean, about 1 hour. Cool before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Old-Fashioned Persimmon Pudding
raw_recipe.description: This is an old-fashioned persimmon pudding recipe, not a cold and creamy pudding. It's very moist, similar to the consistency of pumpkin pie filling.
raw_recipe.name: Old-Fashioned Persimmon Pudding

review.reviewBody: Great recipe! My father-in-law loves persimmon pudding. He gave this a good review.

Just made this and it turned out beautifully. I've never cooked with persimmons before. My persimmons were not ripe, so I peeled them and microwaved them with water for a few minutes. Then used an immersion blender to make puree, rather than pulp. It all came together perfectly. Can't wait to dig in.

Amazing. So tasty. Melted in my mouth.Easy to follow recipe.
I had a bowl of fuyu persimmons that yelled 3 cups of pulp I used in the recipe. I also added a teaspoon of vanilla to the melted butter. 
I have a child with severe food allergies(wheat,eggs,dairy and oat to name a few) I used to love to bake and now its like I'm learning all over again. Some recipes do not fair well with substitutes. This recipe was very forgiving and absolutely delicious. 
I used king Arthur's gluten free baking flour. Trader Joe's thick coconut cream for milk. Apple sauce for eggs. And earth balance whipped vegan butter spread in place of butter. I also used a little bit of the earth balance cinnamon spread because I didn't have enough vegan butter on hand. I just cut back on cinnamon in recipe. So good. Absolutely a main stay in my recipe book from now on. And the family loved it! I'll be making this for the holidays. Can't wait to try with the other variety of persimmons.
Very good. Made non-dairy with vegan butter and almond milk.

Very easy to make. Comes out cake like I think it does better with time. Also I used 3c persimmon due to not wanting to toss the extra ??. Also I got sidetracked during the mixing of the eggs and milk and I beat the devil out of them...
Used Asian persimmons rom my garden, and didn't fully puree completely. Great to start with, and even better served cold the next day after being refrigerated overnight!
4 cups of flour does not a pudding make!! That makes a cake. The best I've had did not have over a cup and a quarter of flour. I can see why this recipe gets bad marks!

People who don't generally like persimmon pudding like this. Or, at least this person does. It's bread-ier than others I've tried, which makes all the difference for me. I also think I used less than the 2 1/2 C pulp called for in the recipe. I had a 16-ounce container I'd bought at the local Farmers Market and just used it. I think this may have also helped with the "more bread than pudding" consistency. Unfortunately mine didn't get the lovely cracks on top like the one in the top photo, so I don't feel it's worthy of posting a picture. But we love it, and isn't that all anyone wants when they try something new?

Thanks for posting! You made a family in Indiana very happy. :-)

This recipe was tasty but the amount of flour in this recipe is completely wrong. It didn’t look right when I looked up the recipe, the batter smelled like flour, and the recipe in the pudding was to dense and rubbery. Adjust the flour and the recipe will be great
This recipe worked well! I re-sized it, as I only had 3 persimmons, which yielded just over a cup of puree. My kids (10 and 7) loved it.
It was better than I thought it would be. The result was not too sweet and it was more like cake than a pudding. However, the taste was excellent. I will make this again.

We found it to be rather tasteless and unexciting. The description says it has the consistency of pumpkin pie, but it’s more like a moist, tasteless sweet bread. The recipe makes far too much. Supposedly serves 12, but my family of 5 barely put a dent in it. I hate to throw it out, but no one really cares to eat it. Such a waste!
Make this every year with persimmons from trees in our yard. Peeling and milling for the pulp is worth it for the end result. Delicious
This is my first time making this. We absolutely loved it. Great recipe, not "wet" like I have had from other people. Got the fruit from my own tree which made it a very satisfying endeavor.

My grandma had a persimmon tree in her yard. She used to gather the persimmons and make pudding. She didn’t have a recipe she wrote down, she just knew it by heart. This recipe tastes so close to what she made! The consistency, texture, and taste of this recipe are near perfection!

I made this and it was great! Glad to have a good recipe for persimmons.
I may have cooked it a little too long, because it was more like cake.
Rick
I made this exactly as written and it was wonderful!
Second time making this. I like it better than the persimmon pudding I grew up with. It is a little less sweet and sticky and the texture is more of what I would expect from a baked pudding.
Very nice dessert. Easy to make.
